brief: MS says the earnings cycle, recovering since the rolling recession ended in April 2025, has moved from early-cycle to mid-cycle, a call MS first made in July: growth stays healthy but decelerates, from 34% EPS growth in 2026 to 14% in 2027 and 9% in 2028, as the Fed normalizes toward less accommodative policy. The correction since June, driven partly by MS's June call for Semis to underperform as revisions breadth peaked, has brought the S&P 500 to MS's 7,100-7,300 support range, a springboard for a new 12-month price target of 8,700 (19x 2028 EPS of $458). Supporting factors: lower oil (Brent to $75/bbl by 4Q27), stabilizing rates, broadening AI adoption (44% of S&P 500 companies cite a quantifiable AI benefit, up from 32% a year ago), and valuation at 18x forward versus MS's 19.5x fair-value estimate. Main risk: a more hawkish Fed re-tightening financial conditions. Bull case 10,000, bear case 6,000 (a 2028 earnings recession). MS recommends staying in Quality but rotating more cyclically, naming Industrials top pick, with Financials, Consumer Discretionary and Hyperscalers also attractive. Separately, MS maps $1.6T of hyperscaler/neocloud AI capex, now including lease capex, to AI supply-chain revenue.
